rubric_items.reason: Covers the api, web and db modules, GET /api/patients, and the appointment and patient tables. It never mentions appointment_event, which becomes relevant if the req-step timestamp question (Q-01) is answered 'time marked Completed'.
Every module, symbol, API, table, column and index id it uses exists in the generated facts and is cited. All 15 claims check out.

Covers other callers of the API (Q-02), background jobs (none), the shared list query (paging, search, sort, Next appointment) and the medical-history leak risk. The appointment_event reader that depends on the req-step answer is not covered.
Known and assumed match req.md. Assumed items REQ-13, 14 and 15 keep their bases. The two unknowns are tied to non-blocking tech-lead questions with defaults.
Readable, and the summary lists the risks. The 'Impacted modules' section also lists the API, the tables and jobs under a modules heading.

findings.text: The impact assumes starts_at (REQ-13) without flagging that req-step Q-01 (start time vs time marked Completed) is still open. If the PO picks completion time, appointment_event becomes a reader and the index argument no longer holds.

cites.quote: Which timestamp defines the Last visit date, the appointment start time or the time staff marked it Completed?

findings.suggested_fix: Add a conditional note: if completion time is chosen, read the completion time from appointment_event and check index support for that read.
